page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-8 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, the instance allocates 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core on a dedicated basis. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include local NVMe storage or bundled GPUs, and it is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU tests placing the instance in the top 25% of evaluated servers. Multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth operations fall within the average range. Specifically, the instance achieves a stress-ng multi-core score of 11559.23 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 6531.0. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 553.27 GB/sec and an uncached large block write speed of 32.75 GB/sec. Static web serving throughput is measured at 10.68 GB/sec, while LLM inference speeds for a small 135M model reach 499.45 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 221.85 tokens/sec for text generation.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c2d-standard-8 offers a balanced resource density of 4.0 GB of memory per core, leveraging dedicated AMD EPYC hardware to deliver consistent compute performance without the overhead of shared-core architectures. The lack of local storage represents a tradeoff, making the instance reliant on external storage solutions. The hardware profile and benchmark results align with workloads such as web serving, software compilation, text processing, and moderate multi-threaded computational tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-8 is an x86_64 virtual machine instance configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It features 4 physical cores with hyper-threading, 32 MB of L3 cache, and lacks local storage or GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks show strong single-core CPU capabilities, placing in the top 25% in stress-ng testing, while multi-core performance, memory bandwidth, and web serving throughput remain in the average tier. With a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this instance provides a stable, dedicated compute environment. It is suited for workloads such as web serving, software compilation, and general-purpose application hosting that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration.
